concerns.text: FR-004 requires translation error to be computed against an EXHAUSTIVE OPTIMAL plan on a sampled subset. The plan repeatedly claims this ('FR-004's exhaustive optimal planner on a sampled subset provides the true ground truth') but NO phase, task, or code module implements the exhaustive planner — Phase 1 only runs the greedy reference_engine, and Phase 2-d defines translation_error purely as 'disagreement with the deterministic ground_truth_plan' (the greedy heuristic). The construct being measured is agreement-with-heuristic, not correctness, exactly the flaw the prior reviewer flagged. Add an explicit exhaustive-optimal-planner task and a validation step comparing greedy vs optimal on the sample.

concerns.text: FR-009/SC-002 require Precision@10, and the plan records it, but nowhere is a RELEVANCE GROUND TRUTH defined for the synthetic queries. Synthetic multi-hop queries have no labeled relevant documents, so Precision@10 is undefined/meaningless without specifying how relevance is determined (e.g., queries constructed so the answer set is known by construction). Without this, SC-002's 'Precision@10 difference ≤ 0.02' cannot be validly evaluated.

SC-001 requires the slope ratio (graph vs. text, via simple linear regression on mean latency per depth) > 1.5 as a conjunctive confirmation criterion, but Phase 3's statistical analysis (ANOVA, Tukey, chi-square, sensitivity sweep) never includes this slope-ratio computation. The plan as written cannot confirm or refute SC-001's second conjunct.

Baseline overhead calibration (FR-010) runs a single trivial query per engine and subtracts it. A single measurement is a noisy estimator of engine overhead; specify repetition (e.g., median of N trivial runs) so corrected_latency_ms is not dominated by one-off scheduler noise.
